result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would eliminate the illusion of separation—the belief that we are fundamentally divided from one another, from nature, and from the deeper currents of life. I would replace it with an unshakable recognition that we are all interconnected, that every act of kindness, cruelty, creation, or destruction ripples outward in ways we can’t always see. This shift wouldn’t erase conflict or difference, but it would make empathy, cooperation, and long-term thinking the default rather than the exception.

It would mean teaching from childhood that our well-being is tied to the well-being of others and the planet—that true freedom isn’t the absence of limits, but the wisdom to live within them. And it would demand that we redesign systems (economic, political, social) to reflect this truth, so that no one is left behind in the name of progress.

In short: I would change the story we tell ourselves about who we are. Because once that story changes, everything else follows.
